Step 2: blocking the earlier occurrences of one transition¶

In plain words¶

For each source transition S: in the selected heads, forbid all attention to the earlier words produced by S. Then measure, for every transition T, how much the probability of the correct next word changes, compared with the same run through the same heads and the same attention code with nothing blocked (paired per run, ± SE). One map per head set: rows = which transition was blocked (S), columns = which transition is predicted (T). Red = worse.

Reading it:

  • A red diagonal (blocking S hurts predicting S, not the others) = these heads retrieve each transition from its own earlier occurrences: the attention is the memory route of that transition.
  • Red rows that hurt everything = the blocked words matter in general, not as a memory of their transition.
  • Controls: blocking the same number of random earlier words (random positions), and blocking S in 16 random heads. If the diagonal is specific, it shows up for the induction heads and not for these.

The diagonal score per head set: mean effect on the diagonal minus mean effect off the diagonal, per run (more negative = more transition-specific), ± SE.

In [42]:
def tm_cache_name(name, grammar):
  return f"transition_memory/{lens_cache_name(grammar.lower())}_{name}_n{N_RUNS_TM}"


stream_infos = {g: {input_key(p): stream_info(p, g) for p in tm_prompts[g]} for g in ("AGL", "SRTT")}


def run_tm_condition(name, heads, grammar, make_mask):
  """make_mask(info) -> (T, T) bool. Returns (runs x transitions) P(correct), final output, last-1000 window."""
  cache = {}

  def builder(key):
    if make_mask is None:  # no-block baseline: same attention code path, nothing blocked
      stream_infos[grammar][key]  # still checks that the run is one of ours
      return None
    if key not in cache:
      cache.clear()
      cache[key] = make_mask(stream_infos[grammar][key])
    return cache[key]

  if heads:
    with knockout(heads, builder):
      results_ = run_lens_extraction(model, tokenizer, tm_prompts[grammar], [NUM_LAYERS], cache_name=tm_cache_name(name, grammar))["logit"]
  else:
    results_ = run_lens_extraction(model, tokenizer, tm_prompts[grammar], [NUM_LAYERS], cache_name=tm_cache_name(name, grammar))["logit"]
  return per_transition_probs(results_, tm_prompts[grammar], grammar)


_tm_baselines = {}


def tm_baseline(head_set_name, heads, grammar):
  """The paired baseline of a head set: the same runs through the same custom-attention code path, nothing blocked.
  (Comparing against the plain model instead would mix in tiny rounding differences between the two code paths.)"""
  if (head_set_name, grammar) not in _tm_baselines:
    _tm_baselines[(head_set_name, grammar)] = run_tm_condition(f"{head_set_name}_noblock", heads, grammar, None)
  return _tm_baselines[(head_set_name, grammar)]


# End-to-end check of the per-run mask (input -> key -> stream -> mask -> attention) on one run, also timed.
probe_inputs = prepare_lens_inputs(tokenizer, tm_prompts["AGL"][0])
with knockout(GROUP_HEADS, lambda key: None):
  free = extract_lens_logprobs(model, probe_inputs, [NUM_LAYERS])["logit"]["logprobs"]
started = time.time()
with knockout(GROUP_HEADS, lambda key: mask_same_transition(stream_infos["AGL"][key], "all")):
  blocked = extract_lens_logprobs(model, probe_inputs, [NUM_LAYERS])["logit"]["logprobs"]
seconds_per_run = time.time() - started
assert not np.allclose(free, blocked), "the per-run mask did not reach the attention"
print(f"[sanity] per-run mask reaches the attention: blocking all same-transition occurrences in the group moves the "
      f"output by up to {np.abs(free - blocked).max():.2f} (log-prob)")
n_transitions = len(TRANSITION_ORDER["AGL"]) + len(TRANSITION_ORDER["SRTT"])
n_baselines = 2 * (2 + len(SINGLE_HEADS))
print(f"{seconds_per_run:.1f} s per run with knockout attention. Estimated: group + controls "
      f"{3 * n_transitions * N_RUNS_TM * seconds_per_run / 3600:.1f} h, Step 3 {8 * N_RUNS_TM * seconds_per_run / 3600:.1f} h, "
      f"single heads {len(SINGLE_HEADS) * n_transitions * N_RUNS_TM * seconds_per_run / 3600:.1f} h, no-block baselines "
      f"{n_baselines * N_RUNS_TM * seconds_per_run / 3600:.1f} h (minus anything already saved)")


def effect_matrix(head_set_name, heads, grammar, mask_fn, baseline_name):
  """Rows: blocked source transition S; columns: predicted transition T. Mean paired change (vs. the no-block
  baseline of the same heads) and SE."""
  order = TRANSITION_ORDER[grammar]
  base = tm_baseline(baseline_name, heads, grammar)
  means, ses, per_run = {}, {}, {}
  for i, S in enumerate(order):
    df = run_tm_condition(f"{head_set_name}_S{i}", heads, grammar, lambda info, S=S, i=i: mask_fn(info, S, i))
    per_run[S] = df.values - base.values
    means[S], ses[S] = paired_change(df, base)
  return pd.DataFrame(means).T.loc[order], pd.DataFrame(ses).T.loc[order], per_run


def diagonal_score(per_run, order):
  """Per run: mean diagonal effect minus mean off-diagonal effect. Returns mean, SE."""
  stack = np.stack([per_run[S] for S in order], axis=1)  # (runs, S, T)
  diag = np.stack([stack[:, i, i] for i in range(len(order))], axis=1).mean(1)
  off = np.array([[stack[r, i, j] for i in range(len(order)) for j in range(len(order)) if i != j] for r in range(stack.shape[0])]).mean(1)
  score = diag - off
  return score.mean(), score.std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(len(score)) if len(score) > 1 else 0.0


def plot_effect_maps(maps, title):
  fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(16, 6.2), gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [11, 9]})
  from matplotlib.colors import TwoSlopeNorm
  for ax, (grammar, (mean, se)) in zip(axes, maps.items()):
    limit = max(np.nanmax(np.abs(mean.values)), 1e-6)
    im = ax.imshow(mean.values, cmap='RdBu', norm=TwoSlopeNorm(vcenter=0, vmin=-limit, vmax=limit), aspect='auto')
    marks = np.abs(mean.values) > SIGNIFICANT_SE * se.values
    for i, j in zip(*np.nonzero(marks)):
      ax.text(j, i, "*", ha='center', va='center', fontsize=9)
    for k in range(len(mean)):
      ax.add_patch(plt.Rectangle((k - 0.5, k - 0.5), 1, 1, fill=False, edgecolor='#0b0b0b', linewidth=0.8))
    ax.set_xticks(range(len(mean.columns)))
    ax.set_xticklabels(mean.columns, rotation=60, ha='right', fontsize=8)
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(mean.index)))
    ax.set_yticklabels(mean.index, fontsize=8)
    ax.set_xlabel("predicted transition (T)")
    ax.set_ylabel("blocked transition (S)")
    ax.set_title(f"{grammar}: {title}")
    fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, shrink=0.8, label="change in P(correct next word)")
  fig.tight_layout()
  plt.show()

[sanity] per-run mask reaches the attention: blocking all same-transition occurrences in the group moves the output by up to 3.73 (log-prob)
11.5 s per run with knockout attention. Estimated: group + controls 1.9 h, Step 3 0.3 h, single heads 2.6 h, no-block baselines 0.4 h (minus anything already saved)

tm_results = {}
for label, heads, mask_fn, base in (("group16", GROUP_HEADS, lambda info, S, i: mask_block_source(info, S), "group16"),
                                    ("group16_randompos", GROUP_HEADS, lambda info, S, i: mask_block_random(info, S, seed=1000 + i), "group16"),
                                    ("random16", RANDOM_GROUP_HEADS, lambda info, S, i: mask_block_source(info, S), "random16")):
  tm_results[label] = {}
  for grammar in ("AGL", "SRTT"):
    print(f"=== {label}, {grammar}")
    tm_results[label][grammar] = effect_matrix(label, heads, grammar, mask_fn, base)

titles = {"group16": "top-16 induction heads: block S", "group16_randompos": "control: top-16, block random positions",
          "random16": "control: 16 random heads, block S"}
for label in ("group16", "group16_randompos", "random16"):
  plot_effect_maps({g: tm_results[label][g][:2] for g in ("AGL", "SRTT")}, titles[label])

def diagonal_table(labels):
  rows = []
  for label in labels:
    for grammar in ("AGL", "SRTT"):
      mean, se, per_run = tm_results[label][grammar]
      order = TRANSITION_ORDER[grammar]
      d, d_se = diagonal_score(per_run, order)
      rows.append({"head set": label, "grammar": grammar, "mean effect on diagonal": np.mean(np.diag(mean.values)),
                   "mean effect off diagonal": mean.values[~np.eye(len(order), dtype=bool)].mean(),
                   "diagonal score": d, "± SE": d_se})
  return pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index(["head set", "grammar"])

display(diagonal_table(["group16", "group16_randompos", "random16"]).round(4))

Step 3: most recent vs. older occurrences (group of 16)¶

In plain words¶

For every predicted word, block in the group of 16 only the most recent earlier occurrence of the same transition, all older ones (keeping the most recent), or all of them; plus a control blocking as many random earlier words of other transitions. Bars: mean change in P(correct next word) per transition (± SE).

Reading it: if blocking only the most recent occurrence hurts as much as blocking all of them, the heads copy the last occurrence. If blocking the older ones hurts while the most recent one is kept, the heads pool many earlier occurrences, closer to counting how often each continuation happened.

In [44]:
recency_results = {}
for mode in ("recent", "older", "all", "random"):
  for grammar in ("AGL", "SRTT"):
    df = run_tm_condition(f"group16_same_{mode}", GROUP_HEADS, grammar, lambda info, mode=mode: mask_same_transition(info, mode, seed=7))
    recency_results[(mode, grammar)] = paired_change(df, tm_baseline("group16", GROUP_HEADS, grammar))

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(17, 4.6), gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [11, 9]})
mode_colors = {"recent": "#eb6834", "older": "#2a78d6", "all": "#0b0b0b", "random": "#9a9a9a"}
mode_labels = {"recent": "most recent only", "older": "all older (keep most recent)", "all": "all earlier occurrences",
               "random": "control: random earlier words"}
for ax, grammar in zip(axes, ("AGL", "SRTT")):
  order = TRANSITION_ORDER[grammar]
  x = np.arange(len(order))
  width = 0.2
  for k, mode in enumerate(("recent", "older", "all", "random")):
    mean, se = recency_results[(mode, grammar)]
    ax.bar(x + (k - 1.5) * width, mean[order], width=width, yerr=se[order], capsize=2, color=mode_colors[mode], label=mode_labels[mode])
  ax.axhline(0, color='#52514e', linewidth=1)
  ax.set_xticks(x)
  ax.set_xticklabels(order, rotation=45, ha='right')
  ax.set_ylabel("change in P(correct next word)")
  ax.set_title(f"{grammar}: blocking same-transition occurrences in the top-16 heads")
  ax.grid(alpha=0.25, axis='y')
axes[0].legend(fontsize=8)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
display(pd.DataFrame({(mode_labels[m], g): {"mean change": recency_results[(m, g)][0].mean(), "mean SE": recency_results[(m, g)][1].mean()}
                      for m in ("recent", "older", "all", "random") for g in ("AGL", "SRTT")}).T.round(4))

Step 2b: the block-18 heads one at a time¶

Same as Step 2a, for each block-18 head alone. Because these heads are redundant (05_head_specialization), single-head effects may be small; the question is whether each head's pattern (which S hurts which T) differs.

In [45]:
for l, h in SINGLE_HEADS:
  label = f"head{l}.{h}"
  tm_results[label] = {}
  for grammar in ("AGL", "SRTT"):
    print(f"=== {label}, {grammar}")
    tm_results[label][grammar] = effect_matrix(label, [(l, h)], grammar, lambda info, S, i: mask_block_source(info, S), label)
  plot_effect_maps({g: tm_results[label][g][:2] for g in ("AGL", "SRTT")}, f"head {l}.{h} alone: block S")

display(diagonal_table(["group16", "group16_randompos", "random16"] + [f"head{l}.{h}" for l, h in SINGLE_HEADS]).round(4))

# Who remembers which transition: the diagonal effect of each head set, per transition
for grammar in ("AGL", "SRTT"):
  order = TRANSITION_ORDER[grammar]
  table = pd.DataFrame({label: pd.Series(np.diag(tm_results[label][grammar][0].values), index=order)
                        for label in tm_results}).round(4)
  print(f"{grammar}: change in P(correct) for transition T when its own earlier occurrences are blocked")
  display(table)

How to interpret the results¶

  • Step 1, strong diagonal in the reading map → the heads look up the earlier occurrences of the very transition being predicted. Off-diagonal mass (e.g. on all exits of the same state) → they read a broader context.
  • Step 2a, red diagonal for the top-16 heads but not for the two controls → these heads' attention is the memory route of each transition: predicting T depends on reading T's own earlier occurrences, through these heads. Whole red rows → the blocked words matter in general (as context), not as the memory of their transition.
  • Step 2b, different single heads with different diagonal cells → specific heads carry specific transitions; the same weak pattern in every head → a shared, redundant mechanism (as in 05 for SRTT).
  • Step 3: most-recent blocking ≈ all-occurrence blocking → copying the last occurrence (expected for SRTT); older-occurrence blocking matters → pooling over many occurrences, closer to counting (expected for AGL if the heads estimate probabilities).
